qualification: local pinned-fixture correctness and production-admission recovery evidence; not hardware, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

priorFailure.interpretationBeforeIsolation: The read-only CR3 admission reproduced the same NX init-text fetch as unrelated memory-writing candidates, leaving the causal mechanism unknown.

isolatedCoherencyFailure.trigger: A write to any protected guest code page made its complete host allocation granule writable and advanced the shared code-protection generation.
isolatedCoherencyFailure.missingBoundary: When an unchanged resident block survived byte-fingerprint validation, or an unchanged shared block was reused, the executor republished it without restoring translated-code protection.
isolatedCoherencyFailure.unsafeState: The block could remain writable while an older inline write-TLB entry still named the same host granule. A later native store could then modify guest code without another protection fault or code-generation advance, leaving stale native translation lookup-visible.
isolatedCoherencyFailure.repair: Fresh compilation, byte-validated resident reuse, and shared-code reuse now all pass through one protection boundary. When protection changes, the executor flushes translation TLB entries and records the new protection generation before publishing the native block.
isolatedCoherencyFailure.scope: This repairs a general self-modifying-code coherency boundary; it is not specific to the CR3 instruction or either measured CR3 site.

regressionCoverage: An inline sibling write unprotects a shared host granule; unchanged byte revalidation must re-protect it, revoke the old write-TLB entry, and recompile after a second write changes the target bytes.
Shared-code reuse restores protection after a sibling mutation before publishing the unchanged block.
verification.focusedGate: 44 tests in DoryARM64Tier1JITTests passed after restoring the CR3 admission; the exact new reprotection regressions also pass.
verification.dbtAndPCGate: 1,444 tests in 171 suites passed; the pinned PVH environment test skipped because its environment variables were absent.

restoredAdmission.boundedRule: Only long-mode CPL0 reads of CR3 are admitted; other control-register reads, all control-register writes, and user-mode reads continue through the interpreter.
restoredAdmission.implementation: The explicit readControlRegister IR reads the immutable dispatch-entry CR3 snapshot at context ABI word 50 in both native tiers and invalidates optimizer knowledge at the read boundary.

interpretation: The unchanged CR3 admission failed with the old lookup/protection boundary and completed the authenticated workload after the isolated reprotection fix. Together with the exact regressions, this supports the stale write-TLB/code-page protection path as the cause of the repeated NX init-text failures and admits the bounded CR3-read lowering. A04.3 and A05.2 remain open for their broader plan checks.
limitations: The complete workload evidence contains one recovery run on one local Apple M2 Pro.
The causal claim combines an exact synthetic reproduction with an A/B source change and production recovery; no host fault trace captured the original silent stale write itself.
The raw diagnostic remains a local build artifact because it includes host-local paths and a large console transcript.
This evidence does not close the named A04.3 SMC corpus or establish a performance delta.
